title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover defrag heuristics v27
author: Daniel Park
description:
Context: KV cache fragmentation and inefficient spillover under mixed-length workloads have been contributing to elevated tail latency and higher-than-expected NVMe IO in multi-tenant Dedicated clusters. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to the KV cache memory manager and eviction pipeline: adaptive eviction priority, fragmentation-aware compaction triggers, hierarchical paging (GPU RAM -> host RAM -> NVMe), and spillover scheduling heuristics to reduce IO amplification.

Design summary: - Adaptive eviction: eviction priority is computed from recency, access weight (per-model/token frequency), and estimated fragmentation contribution. Hot prefixes are promoted; cold fragmented ranges are targeted for compaction + eviction. - Defrag heuristics v27: compact candidate selection uses a lightweight scan of free/used run-lengths and selects slots where compaction reduces future fragmentation score by a threshold. Compaction is bounded by a per-GPU budget to avoid interfering with inference. - Hierarchical paging + spillover: when GPU memory is exhausted, KV pages are first paged to host RAM (zero-copy where supported) and then selectively to NVMe if host pressure remains. Spillover jobs are scheduled via the existing scheduler with a low-priority IO lane; we added backoff to avoid saturation in multi-tenant scenarios. - Continuous batching and kernel interactions: we added a short pause window for compaction tasks aligned with batching windows to avoid degrading tail latency; kernel selection hints are emitted so the runtime avoids launching heavyweight kernels while defrag is active. - Observability: added metrics (kv.compaction.{attempts,succeeded,bytes_moved}, kv.eviction.{counts,reason}, kv.spillover.{to_host,to_nvme}, kv.fragmentation.score) and tracing spans around compaction and spill operations.

Testing & results: - Unit + integration tests for eviction order, compaction correctness, and hierarchical paging paths. - Load tests on perf-canary cluster with mixed short/long sequences showed 12% reduction in 99th percentile latency for large-sequence requests and a 36% reduction in NVMe write amplification under steady-state. - Safety: compaction is gated behind a feature flag (kv.defrag.v27) and an operator-configurable budget.

Rollout plan: 1) feature flag enabled in a handful of canary hosts; 2) monitor kv.fragmentation.score, kv.spillover.to_nvme, and tail latency; 3) gradually enable across Dedicated pools with default budgets, tune budgets per-pool.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Perf benchmarks against perf-canary
- [x] Metrics and dashboard patches
- [x] Feature flag + config knobs

Notes: This PR touches low-level memory manager and scheduler hooks; reviewers please focus on: concurrency safety in compaction loops, correctness of hierarchical paging fallbacks, and potential SLO regressions when compaction runs under high load.

review_comments: Priya Kapoor: Can you clarify the concurrency model for compaction? It looks like the scanner can overlap with eviction; how do you avoid double-free?

Daniel Park (reply): The scanner only marks candidates with an in-place reservation token. Eviction checks for the reservation flag and skips reserved ranges. Added extra assertions and a test (defrag_concurrency_test) to cover overlap. See commit 7b1c4fa.
Liam Chen: The NVMe path could still saturate under multi-tenant burst. Do we need a global IO budget?

Daniel Park (reply): We added a scheduler-level IO lane with backoff and a per-pool IO budget. Defaults are conservative; operators can tune per-pool. Added metrics for queue depth and backoff counters.
Ava Martinez: Observability looks good. Please ensure dashboard uses new metrics and annotates feature flag state so we can correlate regressions.
Daniel Park (reply): Dashboard updated (deploy/observability/dashboards/kv_cache.json) and docs/metrics/kv_cache.md includes recommended alerts.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction prioritization, fragmentation-aware compaction heuristics (v27), hierarchical paging (GPU->host->NVMe) with scheduler-backed spillover to reduce NVMe write amplification and tail latency. Feature gated behind kv.defrag.v27.
